openTomorrow: Yeah, I'll open it tomorrow. I'm curious to see if I can actually stick with this. Day 1 is done, so there's momentum now.
secured: It means I completed today's task and locked in my streak. The app is securing my commitment for the day.
freeze: I think it's like a safety valve - if you mess up, you can freeze your streak instead of losing it completely. Kind of a get-out-of-jail card.
selfReported: That's when you tell the app yourself that you did something, instead of it being verified by the camera or some other way. You're basically being honest on your own.
best: Honestly? Getting that first task done and seeing the flame icon light up. There's something satisfying about that visual. Makes it feel real.
worst: Having to take a photo as proof. I hate being on camera - I knew that was coming but it still made me uncomfortable. That's why I haven't done it yet.
tellFriend: Maybe, yeah. I'd say 'There's this app called GRIIT that tracks habit streaks and makes you prove it with photos. It's a bit intense, but if you're serious about changing something, it actually works because you can't cheat it.' Though I'd warn them about the camera thing.
